advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Distinguish 'CloudWatch listing succeeded with zero Bedrock series' (a valid $0 reading) from 'listing/data call failed' in _metered_spend, so a genuine zero-usage day does not synthesize spend=THRESHOLD and trip the cap.
evidence: handler.py:319-322: `if not found_series:\n    log.error("CloudWatch Bedrock token metrics unavailable: no per-model series found")\n    return None`
handler.py:506-513: when metered is None and `ce_spend` (0) is not >= THRESHOLD_USD, `spend = THRESHOLD_USD` / `effective_source = 'metered_unavailable'`
handler.py:561: `if spend >= THRESHOLD_USD and not attached:` — trips the deny on the synthesized threshold value

ABSENCE: no liveness signal (e.g. successful ListMetrics/GetMetricData completion with an explicitly-empty result) distinguishes 'listing succeeded, zero usage' from 'listing produced nothing'. A completed listing returning zero series is a valid $0 reading, not an unavailable one.
advisory.finding: _metered_spend cannot distinguish 'CloudWatch metrics genuinely absent because there was zero Bedrock usage' from 'CloudWatch listing returned nothing / instrument failure'. When no per-ModelId series is found, found_series stays False and the function returns None, which the caller treats as 'metered unavailable' and sets spend=THRESHOLD_USD (fail-closed). On a legitimate zero-usage day where CE also reports 0 (< threshold), the cap trips and denies all Bedrock principals for no reason.
scenarios: Account with a real quiet Bedrock day (no invocations) where CE also reads $0 for today — cap trips and denies production principals
New region added to REGIONS that legitimately has no Bedrock metrics yet, combined with the primary region also emitting no series in the query window
advisory.suggested_fix: Track listing success separately from found_series: return 0.0 when list_metrics/get_metric_data completed without error but yielded no series, and reserve None strictly for the ClientError paths.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure the deny can be released at the UTC day boundary even when both spend signals are unavailable, or document that a sustained dual-signal outage keeps the cap latched.
evidence: handler.py:579: `elif any_attached and spend < THRESHOLD_USD and not signal_unavailable:`
handler.py:522: `signal_unavailable = metered_status == "unavailable" or ce_status == "unavailable"`
handler.py:506-513: with metered None and ce unavailable, `spend = THRESHOLD_USD`, so `spend < THRESHOLD_USD` is already False independent of the guard
ABSENCE: no separate time-based release (00:00 UTC) that fires regardless of signal availability; release depends entirely on a fresh under-threshold reading that a sustained outage cannot produce.
advisory.finding: When metered spend is unavailable and CE is also unavailable, the cap trips (spend defaults to THRESHOLD_USD) but the release branch is blocked by `not signal_unavailable`, so once tripped under a dual-signal outage the deny can only be lifted by the 00:00 UTC day rollover logic — yet that release branch is ALSO gated on `not signal_unavailable`. If both signals stay unavailable across a day boundary, an attached deny is never released automatically.
scenarios: CloudWatch and Cost Explorer both erroring for an extended window that spans midnight UTC while the deny is attached — the documented automatic 00:00 UTC lift does not occur

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard _ce_spend_today against a missing/empty Total in the CE ResultsByTime entry, defaulting to 0.0 rather than raising KeyError.
evidence: handler.py:496-504: caller only catches `ClientError`, so a KeyError from an empty Total is uncaught and aborts the handler
advisory.finding: _ce_spend_today reads `results[0]["Total"]["UnblendedCost"]["Amount"]` without guarding that the 'Total' key is present/populated. Cost Explorer DAILY queries can return a ResultsByTime entry whose Total is empty for a day with no matching cost, raising KeyError instead of yielding 0; unlike the ClientError path this is not caught, so it propagates and aborts the whole handler tick (no enforcement runs).
scenarios: A day with no Bedrock cost yet where CE returns a ResultsByTime entry with an empty Total map

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Bound the SSM state payload (or use advanced-tier / drop the rates blob from persisted state) and handle ssm.put_parameter failure so state size cannot silently wedge the cap.
evidence: handler.py:105-106 `ssm.put_parameter(Name=STATE_PARAM, Value=json.dumps(state), Type="String", Overwrite=True)`
handler.py state stores `state["rates"] = rates` (full empirical rate map) plus ce cache/day/warned fields — value grows with number of Bedrock usage types
Standard SSM String parameters are capped at 4KB; advanced-tier (8KB) is not requested and _save_state has no error handling
advisory.finding: The handler persists the full empirical `rates` table together with the rest of state into a standard SSM parameter created with Type="String", which is limited to 4KB. As the per-USAGE_TYPE rate map grows, json.dumps(state) can exceed 4KB and ssm.put_parameter will fail, which is not caught in _save_state — a persistent failure would prevent state (tripped_day, ce cache, warned_day) from ever being saved.

evidence: bedrock_spend_cap.tf:400 `STATE_PARAM   = format("/%s/state", local.bedrock_cap_name)`
bedrock_spend_cap.tf:314-322 grants `ssm:GetParameter`, `ssm:PutParameter` on `.../bedrock-spend-cap/state`
handler.py `_save_state`: `ssm.put_parameter(Name=STATE_PARAM, Value=..., Type="String", Overwrite=True)` creates the parameter at runtime
search_files for `aws_ssm_parameter` in bedrock_spend_cap.tf returned `(no matches)`; the param name is absent from ssm.tf's managed `rebar_secret_params` list
ABSENCE: no aws_ssm_parameter resource declares /bedrock-spend-cap/state anywhere in infra/terraform
advisory.finding: The runtime SSM parameter the Lambda reads and writes (STATE_PARAM = /bedrock-spend-cap/state) has no aws_ssm_parameter declaration in Terraform; the Lambda creates it out-of-band on first run via ssm:PutParameter, leaving an unmanaged live resource — the same state/HCL divergence class this restoration is meant to remove.

evidence: bedrock_spend_cap.tf:215 `name         = format("bedrock-daily-%s", var.bedrock_daily_cap_usd)`
README.md 'Change the cap: set `bedrock_daily_cap_usd` and apply.' — the documented operation triggers the rename/replace
bedrock_spend_cap.tf:214-247 the budget carries the 50/80/100% notifications that would be torn down and rebuilt with it
advisory.finding: The alert budget name embeds the cap value (format("bedrock-daily-%s", var.bedrock_daily_cap_usd)); because aws_budgets_budget name is immutable, changing bedrock_daily_cap_usd forces a destroy-and-recreate of the budget and its notifications rather than an in-place update.
advisory.suggested_fix: Use a fixed name such as `name = "bedrock-daily"` and rely on limit_amount for the value.

evidence: bedrock_spend_cap.tf:372-426 aws_lambda_function.bedrock_spend_cap declares no dead_letter_config and no aws_lambda_function_event_invoke_config
bedrock_spend_cap.tf:442-446 aws_cloudwatch_event_target.bedrock_spend_cap_tick sets no dead_letter_config or retry_policy
ABSENCE: no aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm on the function's Errors/Invocations exists in bedrock_spend_cap.tf
README.md: 'a timeout here means the cap silently stops being enforced' — the failure mode is acknowledged but unmonitored
advisory.finding: The enforcement Lambda and its EventBridge tick have no dead-letter queue, on-failure destination, or error/invocation alarm, so a persistently failing tick silently stops cap enforcement with no signal.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a direct test for _refresh_rates with a multi-period, mixed qty (including qty==0) Cost Explorer response asserting the derived per-token rates.
evidence: tests/infra/test_bedrock_spend_cap_handler.py:232: monkeypatch.setattr(module, "_refresh_rates", lambda: {})
search for `_refresh_rates` in the test file returns only the stub line — no direct test
handler.py `_refresh_rates` builds `rates = {usage_type: cost / qty ... if qty > 0 and cost > 0}` from `ce.get_cost_and_usage` (added lines)
blocking.finding: _refresh_rates is only ever monkeypatched to return {} (load_handler stubs it), so its Cost-Explorer aggregation logic — summing UnblendedCost/UsageQuantity per usage type and computing `cost/qty for ... if qty > 0 and cost > 0` — is entirely untested. A regression that (e.g.) divided by zero, dropped the qty>0 guard, or mis-summed multi-period totals would not be caught.
scenarios: A usage type with qty==0 must be excluded to avoid ZeroDivisionError
Multiple ResultsByTime periods must be accumulated per usage type

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting _normalise strips stacked prefixes (e.g. 'us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6' -> 'claudesonnet46').
evidence: search for `_normalise` in the test file returns (no matches)
handler.py comment: "Loop, not a single pass: ids stack them (\"us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6\" ...) and stripping only the first leaves a vendor name embedded"
search for `RATE_OVERRIDES` in the test file returns (no matches)
handler.py `_rate_for`: `for needle, fragment in RATE_OVERRIDES.items(): if needle in model_id: pin = _normalise(fragment); break`
bedrock_spend_cap.tf: `bedrock_cap_rate_overrides = { "titan-embed-text" = "TitanEmbeddingV2-Text" }`
blocking.finding: _normalise's stacked-prefix stripping loop is never tested, despite a source comment flagging it as load-bearing. A model id such as 'us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6' must have both 'us.' and 'anthropic.' stripped; a regression back to a single-pass strip (leaving 'anthropic' embedded) would break rate matching and go undetected.
merged_from: The RATE_OVERRIDES pin-resolution branch in _rate_for is never tested with a populated override. The Titan-embed pin ('titan-embed-text' -> 'TitanEmbeddingV2-Text') is the explicit motivating case in both handler.py and bedrock_spend_cap.tf, yet no test passes a non-empty RATE_OVERRIDES; the branch `for needle, fragment in RATE_OVERRIDES.items(): if needle in model_id: pin = _normalise(fragment)` is uncovered.
scenarios: Input 'us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6' must normalise without a residual 'anthropic'

evidence: tests/infra/test_bedrock_spend_cap_handler.py:43: values_by_id: dict[str, list[float]] | None = None,
search for `values_by_id` shows it is only referenced inside FakeCloudWatch (lines 43,48,61); no test constructs FakeCloudWatch(values_by_id=...)
handler.py `_metered_spend`: `units_1k = sum(result.get("Values", []) or []) / 1000` then `total += units_1k * _rate_for(model_id, metric_name, rates)`
blocking.finding: The positive path of _metered_spend (pricing CloudWatch token values into dollars via `total += units_1k * _rate_for(...)`) is never exercised: FakeCloudWatch.values_by_id exists but no test passes it, so only the listing-error, data-error, and no-series (None) cases are covered. A regression in the /1000 unit conversion, the `units_1k <= 0` skip, or the per-model rate multiplication would not be detected.
scenarios: A single ModelId series with Values summing to 2000 tokens must yield units_1k=2.0 priced at the resolved rate
A series with zero/negative values must be skipped

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Derive the log-group and SSM-state ARN region from the provider region (e.g. data.aws_region.current.name) instead of hardcoding "us-east-1" in the Lambda IAM policy.
evidence: infra/terraform/bedrock_spend_cap.tf:295-300 `Resource = format("arn:aws:logs:%s:%s:log-group:/aws/lambda/%s:*", "us-east-1", ...)`
infra/terraform/bedrock_spend_cap.tf:317-322 SSM state ARN also hardcodes "us-east-1"
infra/terraform/main.tf:5-7 `provider "aws" { region = var.aws_region }`
infra/terraform/variables.tf:1-5 `variable "aws_region" { ... default = "us-east-1" }` — region is a variable, not fixed
aws_cloudwatch_log_group.bedrock_spend_cap (line 363-364) and the Lambda are created in the provider region, so a non-default region diverges from the hardcoded policy region
dropped.finding: The Lambda IAM policy hardcodes 'us-east-1' in the log-group and SSM-state resource ARNs, but the Lambda, its log group, and the state SSM parameter are all created in the provider region (var.aws_region, default us-east-1). If aws_region is set to any non-us-east-1 value, the execution role loses logs:* and ssm:GetParameter/PutParameter permission on the actual (regional) resources, silently breaking logging and state persistence — i.e. the cap stops enforcing without error.
dropped.suggested_fix: Replace the literal "us-east-1" in the Logs and State statement ARNs with data.aws_region.current.name (add a data "aws_region" "current" {} block) so the granted region tracks var.aws_region.
